passages.original: μέμψαιτο δʼ ἄν τις τὸ προοίμιον ὡς τραγικὸν καὶ περιττὸν καὶ ἐπιλόγῳ μᾶλλον ἐοικός. σξηολιον ιβιδ. π. 353 ρ. ὅρα δὲ πῶς ἐπιλογικῶς ἤρξατο ἀπὸ συνηγόρων ἐκβολῆς, ὥσπερ καὶ ὁ Δημοσθένης.
passages.english: One might find fault with the proem as tragic and overwrought, and more like an epilogue. Scholion, ibid., p. 353 R.: See how he began in the manner of an epilogue, with the expulsion of advocates, just as Demosthenes also [did].
passages.notes: "σξηολιον ιβιδ. π. 353 ρ." is a Latin editorial heading ("scholion ibid. p. 353 R.") transliterated into Greek letters by scanning; it has been rendered as the heading. "ἀπὸ συνηγόρων ἐκβολῆς" (literally "from a casting-out of advocates") is obscure. It may mean an opening that disparages or dismisses the opponent's supporting speakers.
